items.section_heading: Badminton - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: Explain the badminton technique you like most. Why?
items.answer: Taking the forehand grip as the chapter describes it: the player holds the racket head in the non-playing hand with the handle pointing towards the body and the face of the racket perpendicular to the floor, then places the playing hand on the handle just like shaking hands with it, so that a V shape is formed between the thumb and the index finger. The handle rests loosely in the fingers for flexibility, and the grip is shortened and placed nearer to the shaft in order to increase control and accuracy while serving and hitting from the forecourt and mid court. It is used to hit shots on the forehand side of the body and around the head shots. This technique is worth liking because holding grip of a badminton racket is the foundation of playing this game, and holding the racket wrongly will reduce the power and accuracy of the stroke. (The question asks for a personal favourite; this answer keeps to one technique that the chapter itself describes.)

items.section_heading: Gymnastics - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: What is the difference between gymnastics events for men and women?
items.answer: The difference is in the number and the kind of events contested. In artistic gymnastics men compete in six events: floor exercise, pommel horse, still rings/roman rings, vaulting table, parallel bars, and horizontal bar. Women compete on four events: floor exercise, vaulting table, uneven bars, and balancing beam. So the pommel horse, still rings, parallel bars and horizontal bar are contested by men only and the uneven bars and the balancing beam by women only, while the floor exercise and the vaulting table are common to both. In addition, only women compete in rhythmic gymnastics, although a new version of that discipline for men is being pioneered in Japan.
grounding: Men compete in six events. These are floor exercise, pommel horse, still rings/roman rings, vaulting table, parallel bars, and horizontal bar.
Women compete on four events. These are floor exercise, vaulting table, uneven bars, and balancing beam.

items.section_heading: Table Tennis - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: Give three landmarks in the development of table tennis.
items.answer: Three landmarks are: (1) in 1890 David Foster in England patented an action game of Tennis on Table, and one year later John Jaques came out with a game called Gossima; (2) in 1900 a celluloid ball was introduced by Jaques and the game was given the name Ping-Pong; and (3) in 1926 the ITTF (International Table Tennis Federation) was founded with headquarters in Berlin, the year in which the first World Championship of Table-Tennis was held in London and the TTFI (Table-Tennis Federation of India) was formed in Calcutta, now known as Kolkata. A later landmark is that table tennis was introduced in the Olympics in 1988 in Seoul, South Korea.

items.section_heading: Table Tennis - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: Define the terms, drive and smash as used in table tennis.
items.answer: Both are offensive strokes. Drive: the racket is primarily perpendicular to the direction of the stroke, and most of the energy applied to the ball results in speed rather than spin, creating a shot that does not arc much, but it is fast enough to make it difficult to return. Smash: it is executed when the opponent has returned a ball that bounces too high and/or too close to the net; smashing is a large back swing and rapid acceleration imparting as much speed on the ball as possible.

items.section_heading: Table Tennis - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: Write in brief the history of table tennis.
items.answer: The game of Table Tennis probably descended from the game of Royal Tennis, which was played in the medieval era (12th century A.D.), and Table Tennis was probably played with improvised equipment in England during the last quarter of 19th century. David Foster in England patented an action game of Tennis on Table in 1890, and one year later John Jaques came out with a game called Gossima. In 1900 a celluloid ball was introduced by Jaques and the name Ping-Pong was given. The game is controlled by the ITTF (International Table Tennis Federation), founded in 1926 with headquarters in Berlin; the first World Championship of Table-Tennis was held in London in 1926 and the TTFI (Table-Tennis Federation of India) was formed in 1926 in Calcutta, now known as Kolkata. Table tennis was introduced in the Olympics in 1988 in Seoul, South Korea.

items.stem: When does a game point occur in tennis?
items.answer: A game point occurs in tennis whenever the player who is in the lead in the game needs only one more point to win the game. The same terminology is extended to sets (set point), matches (match point), and even championships (championship point).

items.section_heading: Tennis - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: What is a break point in tennis?
items.answer: A break point occurs if the receiver, not the server, has a chance to win the game with the next point. Break points are of particular importance because serving is generally considered advantageous, with the server being expected to win games in which they are serving.

items.section_heading: Tennis - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: How is the scoring done in a tennis match?
items.answer: A tennis match is determined through the best of 3 or 5 sets: women play 3 set matches, while men play 5 set matches, so for men the first player to win three sets wins the match and for women the first player to win two sets wins the match. A set consists of games, and a game, in turn, consists of a sequence of points played with the same player serving. A game is won by the first player to have won at least four points in total and at least two points more than the opponent. The running score of each game is described in a manner peculiar to tennis: scores from zero to three points are described as "love", "15", "30" and "40". If each player has scored at least three points, making the score equal at 40 a piece, it is not called out as "40-40" but as "deuce"; if a player then has one more point than the opponent, the score of the game is "advantage" for the player in the lead. A game point occurs when the player in the lead needs only one more point to win the game, and a break point when the receiver, not the server, can win the game with the next point. In a set, if the leading player wins that game the player wins the set 7-5; if the trailing player wins the game, a tie-break is played, which under a separate set of rules allows one player to win one more game and thus the set, giving a final set score of 7-6. In tournament play, the chair umpire announces the winner of the set and the overall score.
